ussfcu_evelyn_greeting.ai_message: Good morning, Evelyn. 3 compliance signals need your attention before your risk committee. The most urgent: mortgage approval rates for applicants under 30 are running 14 points below the portfolio in one product and state, a fair-lending pattern under Regulation B. This pattern was not visible in any single system. Want me to show you the population behind it?
suggested_chips: What is on the disclosure clock?

ussfcu_evelyn_signal_1_fairlending.ai_message: Fair-lending disparity, and it is the critical one. The approval rate for applicants under 30 is 14 points below the portfolio in one product and one geography — a Colorado mortgage. Under ECOA and Regulation B, age is a protected basis, so a gap this size is exposure worth a documented analysis. It was invisible before because approvals live in MeridianLink, ages and geography in the core, and no report joined them. I reconciled them into one population so you can see it.

ussfcu_evelyn_signal_2_trid.ai_message: Here is what is on the disclosure clock this week. 18 active mortgage files are at risk on the TRID timing rules: Loan Estimates approaching the 3-business-day delivery window, or Closing Disclosures inside the 3-business-day-before-closing rule. Late delivery is a reimbursable finding, so these are the files your team should touch first. I can build the member-specific checklist and calendar for any of them.
suggested_chips: Build a member's disclosure checklist and calendar

ussfcu_evelyn_signal_3_complaints.ai_message: 34 member interactions this month used dissatisfaction language and trigger words — fee, disclosure, discrimination — that may meet the CFPB complaint definition, but were never logged. Normalized for member volume, complaints on this product are up 6% quarter over quarter, and examiners react to trends, not one-off mistakes. That trend is the risk indicator, whether or not any single interaction was logged.

ussfcu_evelyn_complaint_trend.ai_response: Here is the trend, and it is the part examiners actually react to. Complaints on the Colorado mortgage are up 6% quarter over quarter, normalized per 1,000 members so the rise is not just a function of membership growth. That crosses your 5% key-risk-indicator threshold. And it is a pattern, not a one-off: the 34 dissatisfaction-language interactions this month cluster on the same product and the same trigger words, fee and disclosure. The surrounding data is what turns an examiner's question from a finding into a clarification.

ussfcu_evelyn_turn_attrition.user_query: Did we lose the 33 to another lender, and why?

The friction is speed and price transparency, and it shows up as attrition, not just dissatisfaction.
